hints: Focus on oxidation numbers, a redox reaction must show one element oxidised and another reduced.
Check reaction 1 first, Mg goes from 0 to +2 while H goes from +1 to 0, so this one is redox.
Now test Cr in reaction 2 and Cu, C and Cl in reaction 3 for any change in oxidation state to see if they can also be redox.
walkthrough:
**Recall the test for redox**

Redox means oxidation numbers change. Oxidation is an increase in oxidation number, reduction is a decrease. If nothing changes, it is not redox.

**Check reaction 1**

Mg changes from 0 in $\text{Mg}$ to +2 in $\text{MgCl}_2$, so it is oxidised. H changes from +1 in $\text{HCl}$ to 0 in $\text{H}_2$, so it is reduced.

$$\text{Mg(0) } \rightarrow \text{ Mg(+2), H(+1) } \rightarrow \text{ H(0)}$$

**Check reaction 2**

This is chromate to dichromate in acid. Cr is +6 in both $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$ and $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$. K is +1, H is +1 and O is -2 throughout, so no change.

$$\text{Cr(+6) } \rightarrow \text{ Cr(+6): no redox}$$

**Check reaction 3 and conclude**

This is a typical acid plus carbonate reaction. Cu stays +2, Cl stays -1, H stays +1, O stays -2, and C stays +4 in $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ and in $\text{CO}_2$. No oxidation number changes, so no redox.

Only reaction 1 is redox.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean all three are redox. Reactions 2 and 3 show no change in oxidation number, they are acid-base and condensation type changes, not electron transfer.
options.B: Incorrect. Reaction 1 is redox, but reaction 2 is not. Students often think reaction 2 is redox because it involves orange chromate to orange dichromate with a chromium compound, but Cr stays at +6 throughout.
options.C: Incorrect. Neither 2 nor 3 is redox. Reaction 3 is just $\text{CuCO}_3$ reacting with acid to give salt, water and $\text{CO}_2$, with all oxidation states unchanged.
options.D: Correct. Only 1 is redox, with Mg oxidised from 0 to +2 and H reduced from +1 to 0. Reactions 2 and 3 have no change in oxidation numbers.
